§NEW.name: New Instance
§NEW.description: Creates a new instance of a class. The class name goes in braces; constructor arguments use §A. Use §NEW{ClassName} §/NEW for zero-argument constructors.

§B.name: Binding
§B.description: Declares a variable binding. Use ~ prefix for mutable variables. Immutable by default. Give null an explicit existing nullable type, such as string?.

§F.name: Function
§F.description: Defines a standalone function (not a class member). Use for top-level functions or static utility methods.
§F.csharpEquivalent:
public static int Add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
private void Log(string message) { Console.WriteLine(message); }

§AF.name: Async Function
§AF.description: Defines an async function. Use §AF for standalone async functions, §AMT for async class methods.
§AF.csharpEquivalent:
public async Task<string> FetchDataAsync() { ... }
public async Task ProcessAsync() { await DoWork(); }

§M.name: Module
§M.description: Defines a named module for static members. Its functions use §F; C# callers keep the original static class name. Static class declarations with §CL are rejected.

§MT.name: Method
§MT.description: Defines a method within a class. Supports visibility (pub/priv/prot) and modifiers such as virt/vr, over/ov, abs, stat/st, and seal.

§I.name: Input Parameter
§I.syntax: Inline (type:name) parameters in function headers; indented §I{type:name} for delegates and full indexers
§I.description: Header parameter syntax. Modifiers: 'this' (extension method), 'ref', 'out', 'in', 'params'. Default values use =expr in the signature.
§I.csharpEquivalent: Type name, this Type name, ref Type name, params Type[] name, Type name = default

examples.name: Extension Method Parameter
examples.description: Marks this as an extension method parameter (C# 'this' modifier)

§O.name: Output Type
§O.syntax: Inline -> type in function headers; indented §O{type} for delegates
§O.description: Declares the return type of a function or method via the header arrow.

§R.name: Return
§R.description: Returns a value from a function or method. Use bare §R for void returns.

§CL.name: Class
§CL.description: Defines a class. Supports modifiers such as abs, seal, partial, stat, struct, and readonly. Use §EXT for base class and §IMPL for interfaces.

§EXT.name: Extends
§EXT.description: Specifies the base class for inheritance.

§IMPL.name: Implements
§IMPL.description: Specifies an interface the class implements.

§IFACE.name: Interface
§IFACE.description: Defines an interface with method signatures.
§IFACE.csharpEquivalent: public interface IRepository { void Save(Entity e); }

§L.name: Loop
§L.description: For loop with an inclusive integer range. The body is indented under the loop header.

§WH.name: While Loop
§WH.description: Executes body while condition is true.

§DO.name: Do-While Loop
§DO.description: Runs the indented body at least once; the matching closer carries the condition.

§IF.name: If Statement
§IF.description: Conditional branching. §EI for else-if, §EL for else. Both are optional.

§AWAIT.name: Await
§AWAIT.csharpEquivalent:
var result = await FetchAsync();
await Task.Delay(1000);

§TR.name: Try Block
§TR.description: Exception handling. §TR for try block, §CA for catch (with optional type and variable), §FI for finally.

§CA.name: Catch Block
§CA.description: Catches exceptions. Type and variable name are optional.

§TH.name: Throw
§TH.description: Throws an exception. Use §RT to rethrow in a catch block.

§GOTO.name: Goto
§GOTO.description: Jump to a specific case label or to the default case in a switch statement. For regular goto, use §GOTO{labelName}.

§E.name: Effects
§E.description: Declares side effects a function may have. Common effects: cw (console write), db (database), net (network), fs:r/fs:w (file system), rand (random), time, and env. Unresolved external effects are not purity proofs; supply authoritative effect metadata rather than inventing an effect code.

§Q.name: Precondition
§Q.description: Declares a precondition that must be true when the function is called. Part of Design by Contract.

§S.name: Postcondition
§S.description: Declares a postcondition that will be true when the function returns. Use result to refer to the return value.

§PROP.name: Property
§PROP.description: Defines a property with optional getter and setter. Auto-properties use accessor shorthand such as get,set, get,priset, or get,init. Full properties use indented §GET and §SET bodies.

§SET.name: Setter
§SET.description: Property setter with optional visibility modifier.
§SET.csharpEquivalent: set { body } or private set { body }

§FLD.name: Field
§FLD.description: Defines a field in a class. Usually private, prefixed with underscore by convention.

§CTOR.name: Constructor
§CTOR.description: Defines a class constructor. Use §BASE with §A arguments to call a base constructor, or §THIS to chain constructors.
§CTOR.csharpEquivalent:
public User(string name) { _name = name; }
public Admin(string name) : base(name) { }

§THIS.name: This Constructor
§THIS.description: Chains to another constructor in the same class.

§EN.name: Enum
§EN.description: Defines an enumeration. Enum values are indented under §EN and may use = for explicit values.
§EN.csharpEquivalent:
public enum Status { Active, Inactive, Pending }
public enum Priority : byte { Low = 0, High = 1 }

§EVT.name: Event
§EVT.description: Defines an event. Simple form has no body. For custom add/remove accessors, use indented §EADD and §EREM blocks inside the event body.

§EADD.name: Event Add Accessor
§EADD.description: Custom add accessor body inside an event definition (§EVT). Contains statements executed when a handler is subscribed.

§EREM.name: Event Remove Accessor
§EREM.description: Custom remove accessor body inside an event definition (§EVT). Contains statements executed when a handler is unsubscribed.

§LAM.name: Lambda
§LAM.description: Creates an anonymous function using name:type parameter pairs. It can capture variables from its enclosing scope. The closing delimiter carries no source ID. Bind local helpers as lambdas, not nested §F declarations. Automatic local-function conversion lowers noncapturing, non-generic direct same-point calls with ordinary parameters. Direct self-recursion also requires a complete proof of pure built-in scalar operations and captures only the initialized internal self binding; unsupported cases remain explicit converter preservation.
§LAM.csharpEquivalent:
x => x * 2
(a, b) => a + b
items.Where(x => x > 5)

§W.name: Switch/Match
§W.syntax: §W expression with indented §K pattern → result cases; use in an expression context, such as §R §W
§W.description: Pattern matching switch expression. §K introduces each case/pattern. Use _ for default.
§W.csharpEquivalent:
x switch { 1 => "one", 2 => "two", _ => "other" }
shape switch { Circle c => c.Area(), Rectangle r => r.Width * r.Height }

§K.name: Case
§K.description: A case in a switch expression. Use _ for default.

§USE.name: Using/Resource
§USE.csharpEquivalent:
using (var stream = File.OpenRead(path)) { ... }
using var connection = new SqlConnection(connStr);

§WHERE.name: Generic Constraint
§WHERE.description: Constraint on a generic type parameter.

§??.name: Null-Coalescing (Legacy)
§??.description: Legacy tag lookup retained; author infix null-coalescing: left ?? fallback.

§?..name: Null-Conditional Access
§?..description: Legacy tag lookup retained; author postfix null-conditional member access.

§INTERP.name: String Interpolation
§INTERP.description: Plain strings interpolate ${expression}, including numeric expressions. Escape \${0} for literal placeholder text. The legacy section form uses separate literal and §EXP parts.

§C.name: Call
§C.description: Compatibility call lookup retained during integration. Author ordinary calls with postfix parentheses. A section call's manifest effect charge alone does not establish authoritative metadata resolution.

§U.name: Using Import
§U.description: Imports a namespace or creates an alias. Must appear inside a module (§M{Name}) block.
§U.csharpEquivalent: using Namespace; or using Alias = Namespace;

§ARR.name: Array
§ARR.description: Creates a fixed-size array with a typed §ARR value literal. Elements are whitespace-separated; group infix elements explicitly. The documented bare closer remains part of this staged literal form.

§LIST.name: List
§LIST.csharpEquivalent: new List<Type>() or new List<Type> { elements }

§P.name: Print
§P.description: Prints to console with newline. Use §Pf for no newline.

§EACH.name: Foreach
§EACH.description: Iterates over each element in a collection. Type is inferred in §EACH{variable}; §EACH{variable:type} specifies it explicitly. An optional third field names the index.

§IV.name: Invariant
§IV.description: Declares an invariant at module scope.

§PP.name: preprocessor directive
§PP.description: Conditional compilation blocks use §PP for #if and §PPE for #else. Indented statement bodies end at dedent. Nested §PP blocks express #elif. Code inside is conditionally included based on defined symbols.

§ASSIGN.name: variable assignment
§ASSIGN.description: Declare a mutable binding with a ~-prefixed name; use §ASSIGN for all updates, including increments and compound arithmetic.

§IXER.name: indexer definition
§IXER.description: Defines an indexer on a class or interface. Full indexers use indented §I parameters and §GET/§SET/§INIT bodies. Compact auto-indexers use accessor shorthand and inline parameters.

§DEL.name: delegate definition
§DEL.syntax: §DEL{name} with indented §I parameters and optional §O return type
§DEL.description: Defines a delegate type (function signature). Use for callbacks, event handlers, and function references. §DEL can appear at the top level or nested inside §CL class bodies.

§OP.name: operator overload
§OP.description: Defines an operator overload using the supported arithmetic, comparison, equality or unary operators. Updates still use §ASSIGN; do not author increment/decrement or compound assignment expressions.

§RT.name: Rethrow
§RT.description: Rethrows the current exception in a catch block.

§VAR.name: Variable Pattern
§VAR.description: Captures a value into a variable in pattern matching.

§WHEN.name: Guard Clause
§WHEN.description: Adds a guard condition to a pattern match case.

§A.name: Argument
§A.description: Marks a constructor or staged section-call argument. Ordinary calls use comma-separated arguments inside parentheses.

§EX.name: Example
§EX.description: Inline example or test code in documentation.

§SN.name: Since
§SN.description: Documents the version when a feature was introduced.

§DP.name: Deprecated
§DP.description: Marks code as deprecated with a reason.

§BR.name: Breaking Change
§BR.description: Documents a breaking change in the API.

§AS.name: Assume
§AS.description: Documents an assumption that must be true at this point in the code.

§SYNC.name: Synchronization Block
§SYNC.description: Locks an object while executing the indented body.

§EEXT.name: Enum Extension
§EEXT.description: Defines extension methods for an enum type.

§RANGE.name: Range
§RANGE.description: Represents a range value (start..end) for array/span slicing.

§^.name: Index From End
§^.description: Indexes from the end of a collection. Equivalent to C#'s ^n operator.
